clue.text: Possibly fools more stupid son but not daughter

definitions.note: a fool is one kind of pudding, so fools in the plural are examples of the dessert course

indicators.note: says that one letter is taken away from what goes before it

parts.note: dafter means sillier, more stupid

explanation.surface: Someone compares fools, an even sillier son, and leaves the daughter out of it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'but not daughter' removes D from DAFTERS. 'fools' looks like silly people; it is the fruit-and-cream pudding. AFTERS is the British informal word for dessert.
explanation.definitionFit: Afters is a British informal word for the dessert course, and fools are fruit-and-cream desserts, an example of it.

clue.text: Time machine worked, provoking a powerful response

indicators.note: worked suggests something manipulated or kneaded into new shape

explanation.surface: A time machine functioned and caused a strong reaction.
explanation.definitionFit: Anthemic describes rousing music that stirs a big emotional response, like an anthem.

clue.text: Catchy number, maybe? It starts here repeatedly

definitions.text: Catchy number, maybe? It starts here repeatedly

parts.words: Catchy number, maybe? It starts here repeatedly
parts.note: Catch-22 makes the number catchy, and this clue starts at square 2, so repeating that figure gives the number

explanation.surface: A tune that sticks in the head, beginning again and again.
explanation.walkthrough: Catch-22 is Joseph Heller's novel; this clue is 2 down, so its number repeated gives the same figure.
explanation.definitionFit: The number in Catch-22 is the one formed by writing this clue's number twice.

clue.text: Runs over twelve-inch gap

indicators.note: in a down clue the first piece sits over, above, the next

parts.note: R is the cricket abbreviation for runs
twelve inches make one foot, written as 1 FT

explanation.surface: Water running across a foot-wide crack.
explanation.walkthrough: 'twelve-inch' is 1 FT, with the 1 read as the letter I.
explanation.definitionFit: A rift is a crack or split, a gap in rock or in a relationship.

clue.text: Moderate, not hard, persuasive tactics

indicators.note: tells us a letter is left out of the word before it

parts.note: Chambers gives soft-shell as an adjective meaning moderate in policy or principles
H is the pencil abbreviation for hard

explanation.surface: Advice on gentle, unforceful ways to win a customer round.
explanation.walkthrough: 'not hard' takes H out of SOFT-SHELL. The surface reads 'not hard' as describing the tactics; it is the instruction to drop H.
explanation.definitionFit: A soft sell is a gentle approach to selling, persuading a buyer by subtle means rather than pressure.

clue.text: Poems about policeman stifling appeal — they're strange

indicators.note: the poems surround everything else

parts.note: odes are lyric poems

indicators.note: smothering, so the officer wraps round the appeal

parts.note: DI is a detective inspector
it is informal for sex appeal

explanation.surface: Verses about a constable muffling a plea are weird.
explanation.walkthrough: 'they're strange' is the definition: a plural noun phrase standing for things that are strange. 'appeal' is sex appeal, informally.
explanation.definitionFit: Oddities are strange things or people, things that are peculiar.

clue.text: In which you'd eat pastries, for the most part fancy

definitions.text: In which you'd eat pastries, for the most part fancy

indicators.note: fancy as a verb means to imagine, and as an adjective elaborate, signalling a new arrangement
most but not all of the word is used, so its final letter goes

explanation.surface: Gatherings where people munch cakes are mostly elaborate affairs.
explanation.walkthrough: 'for the most part' drops the last S of PASTRIES; 'fancy' rearranges EAT PASTRIE.
explanation.definitionFit: Tea parties are afternoon gatherings where cakes and pastries are served with tea.

clue.text: Possibly overthrow former captain of territorial army division

parts.note: ex means former

indicators.note: a captain heads a team, so the head letter of the next word

parts.note: RA is the Royal Artillery

explanation.surface: An ex-captain of the Territorial Army is perhaps toppled.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket an overthrow is a fielder's wild return that concedes an extra run. The Territorial Army is Britain's army reserve.
explanation.definitionFit: In cricket, runs from an overthrow are scored as extras, so an overthrow is a possible example.

clue.text: Stories about, say, subjects

indicators.note: the stories go round the other letters

parts.note: lies are false stories
eg, for example, is what say means

explanation.surface: Tales about, for instance, topics.
explanation.definitionFit: A liege can be a vassal owing feudal allegiance, so lieges are subjects of a lord.

clue.text: Reportedly gathers flowers

indicators.note: signals that a word is said out loud, giving a different spelling

parts.note: flocks means gathers in crowds

explanation.surface: A rumour of garden blooms.
explanation.definitionFit: Phlox is a genus of garden plants with clusters of bright blooms.

clue.text: Ran into hard times, retiring for the night? Sort of

definitions.note: Twelfth Night is the Shakespeare comedy, so the word is a sort of night

indicators.note: something retiring withdraws, going backwards, so the assembled letters are read in reverse
says the word for ran goes inside the letters for hard times

parts.note: H is the pencil abbreviation for hard, and times gives T twice, T being the multiplication sign's letter
flew means ran or hurried

explanation.surface: Someone who ran into hard times goes to bed early for the night.
explanation.walkthrough: 'into' puts FLEW inside H and TT, giving HTFLEWT, and 'retiring' turns it backwards. Twelfth Night is Shakespeare's play and the eve of Epiphany.
explanation.definitionFit: Twelfth Night is the Shakespeare play and the January feast, so twelfth is a kind of night in the cryptic sense.

clue.text: One forced to join crowd in a river

indicators.note: the word for crowd sits inside the name of the river

parts.note: the Dee is a river in Scotland and another between Wales and England
a raft is informally a large number, a crowd

explanation.surface: A conscript joins a crowd in a river.
explanation.definitionFit: A draftee is a conscript, someone compelled to enlist in the armed forces.

clue.text: Old lizards, initially thought extinct, found scurrying about

definitions.note: newts were once classed with lizards, and the young newt has this archaic name

indicators.note: the picked letters are moved about into a new order
takes the opening letter of each of the four words that follow

explanation.surface: Ancient reptiles, assumed to have died out, are seen scuttling around.
explanation.walkthrough: 'initially' takes T, E, F, S from thought extinct found scurrying, and 'about' rearranges them.
explanation.definitionFit: Eft is an old or dialect word for a newt, formerly loosely counted among the lizards.

clue.text: Weak father no longer builds part of roof for trap

parts.note: soft means weak or feeble
pa is an informal word for father
late means former, no longer living or in office

explanation.surface: A feeble dad who has passed away put up part of a roof as a snare.
explanation.walkthrough: 'trap' is slang for the mouth, so the 'roof' is the roof of the mouth, not of a building.
explanation.definitionFit: The soft palate is the rear part of the roof of the mouth, and trap is slang for mouth.

clue.text: Advance given by gambler and yours truly going over books

indicators.note: in a down clue, me sits above the books

parts.note: a better is one who bets
yours truly means me, the setter
NT is the New Testament, a set of books

explanation.surface: A loan from a punter and the setter covering some volumes.
explanation.definitionFit: Betterment means improvement or advancement.

clue.text: Chieftain flustered after CIA censored line in programme?

indicators.note: agitated or confused, so the remaining letters are put into a fresh order
material censored is cut out, so these three letters are removed

explanation.surface: A tribal leader gets agitated after the CIA silences him.
explanation.walkthrough: 'censored' removes C, I, A from CHIEFTAIN, leaving HEFTN, which 'flustered' rearranges.
explanation.definitionFit: An if-then statement is a conditional instruction, a typical line of computer code.

clue.text: Discarded what is most certainly not right-on

definitions.text: what is most certainly not right-on
definitions.meaning: left is the opposite of right and off the opposite of on, so the phrase is the exact inverse

explanation.surface: Something thrown away is far from politically correct.
explanation.definitionFit: Left off means omitted, and taken literally it pairs the opposites of right and on.

clue.text: Equipped spy to protect journalist following attack

indicators.note: the rest comes after the word for attack

parts.note: a fit is a sudden attack of illness

indicators.note: the spy shelters the journalist inside

parts.note: a tout is a racing tipster who spies on horses in training
ED is short for editor

explanation.surface: A spy is kitted out to guard a reporter after an assault.
explanation.walkthrough: A tout is a racing tipster who spies on horses in training, which is why spy fits.
explanation.definitionFit: Fitted out means equipped or furnished with what is needed.

clue.text: Is unable to dissect animal — bottle needed

indicators.note: cutting into, so the inability splits the animal apart

parts.note: a deer is an animal
can't means is unable to

explanation.surface: A student can't cut up an animal and needs a jar.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Is unable' reads as part of the sentence; it is CAN'T, with the apostrophe ignored.
explanation.definitionFit: A decanter is a glass bottle for serving wine or spirits.

clue.text: Iterated nation is in debt, so to speak?

indicators.note: the nation sits inside the debt

parts.note: red is debt, as in being in the red
a state is a nation

explanation.walkthrough: 'in the red' means in debt, so RED stands for debt; 'so to speak' admits the stretch.

clue.text: Weaklings call for help to secure feminine bow

indicators.note: the distress call holds the other letters fast inside it

parts.note: SOS is the international distress signal
F is the grammatical abbreviation for feminine
a bow is a kind of tie, as in bow tie

explanation.walkthrough: 'bow' looks like a verb or a ship's front; it is the kind of tie.
explanation.definitionFit: Softies are people who are weak or soft-hearted, weaklings in an informal sense.

clue.text: Port that's red

a red is a socialist or left-winger

clue.text: Naturally entertaining universal Asian dance

clue.text: Free gift finally found in children's toy

indicators.note: takes the last letter of the word
